text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT
- The Helsinki Stock Exchange's total market capitalisation increased by almost 100 billion markka in 1996.
- Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen says unemployment will fall if economic growth is above the European average.
- Appeal court eased sentences for three women Finnish animal activists who set free hudreds of farm foxes in May 1995.
- Obesity may become the next epidemic jeopardising health, says Swedish professor. Only 10 percent of Swedes can be classified as "fat" compared to Finland's 30 percent.
KAUPPALEHTI
- Newsprint prices are falling and the highest estimates are for a decline of over 10 percent in some cases. Enso representative says Finnish producers' prices are competitive.
- TT Tieto, Raisio and Cultor have become the most interesting Finnish companies in London, survey of 29 analysts and fund managers shows. OKOBANK and Finnair least interesting.
DEMARI
- The government's budget for jobs for the unemployed for next year is 345 million markka smaller than this year's -- the money will create jobs for 14,500.
- Neste and Borealis receive permission to emit wastewater outside Porvoo in southern Finland.
- Social democrat MPs close to trade unions say they are not an organised wing within the party, but cooperate particularly on labour market issues.
HUFVUDSTADSBLADET
- More hotels planned in Helsinki although profitability is poor despite improved capacity use: entrepreneurs ignore depressed price level, researcher says.
TURUN SANOMAT
- Comprehensive incomes settlement would pave the way the Economic and Monetary Union, says secretary general Seppo Juntila at the Confederation of Salaried Employees in Finland (STTK).
- Five died and several were injured in road accidents in slippery weather on Monday.
AAMULEHTI
- Mobile phones are a symbol of the postmodern era, emphasing individuality, personal focus, job requirements, mobility, stress etc, reasearcher says.
- Finnish truckers fear traffic jams at Russian border will result from new Russian arrangement for granting traffic permits to overweight vehicles.
